lead.hed: Defense News: Army wants 133,000 GMLRS rockets by 2034. A paper is not a factory.
lead.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: an Army sources-sought notice asks industry how to make 133,014 GMLRS rockets by 2034 — 19,002 a year from 2028, first deliveries February 2030. Lockheed is already aiming at 14,000 a year. A white-paper deadline of Sept. 1 is not a signed contract. Stockpiles after Ukraine and Iran are the file.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Army photo by Sgt. Jamie Robinson · DVIDS 8730793 · PUBLIC DOMAIN · HIMARS / GMLRS live fire, Northeast Syria, Oct. 31, 2024
lead.image_note: Official U.S. Army DVIDS still of a GMLRS rocket leaving an M142 HIMARS. Not today's SAM.gov notice. Not a Lockheed factory floor. Not a brand tile. Caption must say 2024 live-fire photo, not a 2026 production line.

political.hed: WORLD: Donalds takes the Florida GOP nod. Nixon takes the DSA Senate lane.
political.insight: WORLD Radio, Wednesday: Byron Donalds won the Republican primary to succeed Ron DeSantis and will face David Jolly. DSA’s Angie Nixon beat Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination and draws Ashley Moody in November. A primary tape is not a general-election map.

political.hed: Law & Liberty: school phone bans are real. Parent screen habits are the gap.
political.insight: Law & Liberty, this week: at least 35 states now limit phones in school; six added screen-time bills this spring. Hess’s point is the parent split — most still want laptops in class. A bell-to-bell rule is not a household reset.

political.hed: Law & Liberty: killing the property-tax bill is not shrinking the government
political.insight: Law & Liberty, Monday: Florida, North Carolina, and Oklahoma are teeing up 2026 property-tax limits. The essay’s test is the 1970s lesson — a cap without a spending rule just moves the burden to fees, aid, and debt. A smaller first bill is not a smaller state.

tech.hed: DARPA’s lift contest hit 3.84-to-1. That is not four times the airframe.
tech.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: DARPA closed the Lift Challenge on Aug. 11. AVIDrone’s Katana, 29.3 pounds, carried 112.4 pounds about five nautical miles and won $1.25 million. Close is not the 4-to-1 goal. A prize flight is not a fielded cargo drone.

tech.hed: Defense News: Unitree’s robot dogs track U.S. Army-funded research
tech.insight: Defense News / Reuters, Tuesday: researchers say Unitree’s Go-series dogs follow Army-backed Mini Cheetah work. The Pentagon listed Unitree as a Chinese military company in June. Open papers are not a sanction. A listing is not a U.S. factory.

tech.hed: Air Force still wants target drones that can mimic stealth jets
tech.insight: Defense News, Monday: an Air Force RFI seeks attritable targets that can play stealth fighters, bombers, and hobby swarms. SAM.gov deadline Sept. 28. QF-16s are not fifth-gen stand-ins. A request for ideas is not a buy.

watch.hed: WATCH: Polar Sentinel steel is up at Bollinger. Still not a delivered cutter.
watch.insight: USNI Monday from Pascagoula: stern sections of the future USCGC Polar Sentinel (WMSP-21) stand nearly four stories. Modules photographed Aug. 5. Yard steel is not ice on the bow. Pin delivery, not the class rendering.

watch.hed: WATCH: Benfold left Yokosuka. The power-loss file is not closed.
watch.insight: USNI Monday: USS Benfold (DDG-65) departed Yokosuka after a scheduled call. She had been towed to Subic after four days without power in the South China Sea. Underway again is not a closed engineering report.
